prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals and commitments

Education and skills
- Make education the top priority. Cut class sizes to 30 or fewer for ages 5–7 by ending the assisted places scheme. Guarantee nursery places for all 4‑year‑olds and set targets for 3‑year‑old provision.
- Focus on standards: baseline assessment, ability-based setting, literacy and numeracy drives (including phonics and whole-class interactive maths), summer literacy schools, and ambitious reading targets.
- Tackle failing schools with “fresh starts,” empower successful schools to take over underperformers, inspect and, if needed, intervene in failing local authorities.
- Expand IT in learning: connect schools to the internet (National Grid for Learning), upskill teachers, quality-grade educational software.
- Strengthen teaching: induction year, a General Teaching Council, recognition for high performers, and faster removal of persistently underperforming staff. Mandatory training for headteachers.
- Reform higher education finance with income‑contingent, fairer repayment of student support; promote lifelong learning through broader A‑levels, stronger vocational routes, Individual Learning Accounts, Investors in People, and a University for Industry.

Economy, tax and public finances
- Prioritise macroeconomic stability with low inflation (around 2.5%), reform monetary policy arrangements, and apply strict fiscal rules (borrow to invest over the cycle; keep debt prudent).
- No rise in basic or top rates of income tax; aim for a lower 10p starting rate; cut VAT on domestic fuel to 5%; keep zero VAT on essentials. Encourage saving and long‑term investment (new ISAs; review corporate/capital gains tax).
- Conduct spending reviews; shift resources from failure to investment. Early “welfare‑to‑work” Budget funded by a windfall levy on privatised utilities.

Business, work and regional growth
- Toughen competition law; regulate utilities effectively. Revive public‑private partnerships and the Private Finance Initiative; give self‑financing public bodies more commercial freedom.
- Support small firms (tackle late payment, cut red tape, high‑tech start‑ups, export help). Create Regional Development Agencies. Back science, design, and green technologies; expand renewables; no new economic case for additional nuclear plants.
- Maintain a flexible labour market with minimum standards, including a sensibly set National Minimum Wage advised by a Low Pay Commission. Facilitate union recognition where a majority of relevant workers vote for it. Promote employee ownership.

Welfare to work
- Get 250,000 under‑25s off benefit into work or training via four options: private-sector jobs (with rebates), voluntary-sector jobs, full‑time study for the unqualified, or an environment taskforce. Replace repeat cautions for youth with a final warning.
- Right to study for under‑18s in work; targeted incentives to hire the long‑term unemployed; Employment Zones with personal job accounts; focused support for lone parents; clamp down on benefit fraud.

Health
- End the internal market; keep planning and provision distinct but cut administrative costs and redirect savings to patient care. Treat an extra 100,000 patients initially; end waits for cancer surgery.
- Primary care‑led commissioning with 3–5‑year hospital agreements; measure outcomes and improve quality (including eliminating mixed‑sex wards). Fix PFI delivery problems; oppose clinical service privatisation. Create an independent food standards agency; ban tobacco advertising. Increase NHS spending in real terms annually.

Crime and justice
- Halve the time from arrest to sentence for persistent young offenders; establish Youth Offender Teams; strengthen parental responsibility orders.
- Decentralise the CPS; set clear sentencing guidelines; extend appeals on unduly lenient sentences; make prisons constructive and tackle drugs (testing and treatment orders). Create new offences for racially motivated crimes; improve victims’ rights. Free vote on banning handguns.

Families, housing, pensions and care
- National childcare strategy; support reasonable limits on excessive working hours, holidays, and parental leave; keep universal Child Benefit to 16 uprated with prices.
- Reinstate investment in social housing by releasing council house receipts; protect tenants (HMO licensing); introduce commonhold; tackle gazumping; duty to protect unintentionally homeless families.
- Retain and price‑link the basic state pension; protect SERPS as an option; develop stakeholder pensions; stronger consumer protection to prevent mis‑selling; Royal Commission on long‑term care; independent inspection and a long‑term care charter.

Environment, transport, culture and sport
- Make every department accountable for environmental outcomes; create a parliamentary environmental audit committee. Develop an integrated transport policy: stronger rail regulation and a new rail authority; a public‑private partnership for London Underground; better local bus regulation and bus lanes; promote low‑emission vehicles; strategic roads review.
- Protect rural services (including the Post Office); reform agricultural policy; widen responsible access to the countryside; strengthen wildlife and animal welfare protections; support angling.
- Establish a National Endowment for Science, Technology and the Arts; stop sell‑offs of school playing fields; reform lottery distribution; consider a not‑for‑profit operator; balance public and commercial broadcasting while safeguarding the BBC. Promote a voluntary citizens’ service.

Constitutional and political reform
- Remove voting rights of hereditary peers as a first step in House of Lords reform; review appointments; modernise the Commons; adopt a Freedom of Information Act; create an independent National Statistical Service; increase transparency of party funding and ban foreign donations; hold a referendum on the voting system.
- Devolution by referendum: a Scottish Parliament with defined powers; a Welsh Assembly with secondary powers; a directly elected mayor and strategic authority for London; regional chambers and, where approved, elected regional assemblies. Strengthen, localise and performance‑manage local government.

Immigration/asylum and Northern Ireland
- Speed and fairness in immigration and asylum decisions; reform outdated rules; regulate advisers; reduce fraud. Support the peace process with measures on rights, policing confidence, equality at work, and economic development.

Europe, defence and international affairs
- Lead EU reform (single market completion, enlargement, CAP/CFP reform, more openness, targeted QMV, retain vetoes on key issues) and sign the Social Chapter. Decide on the single currency by economic tests, with any entry requiring Cabinet, Parliament and a referendum.
- Base security on NATO; conduct a strategic defence and security review; retain the nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament; ban anti‑personnel landmines; tighten arms export controls; support defence diversification.
- Reform and strengthen the UN; reinvigorate Commonwealth ties. Create a Cabinet‑level international development department; reverse the decline in aid spending toward the 0.7% target; support fair trade and debt relief; back a permanent international criminal court; lead on climate action (aiming for a 20% CO2 cut by 2010) and a new global climate agreement.
